clue.text: Express disapproval with uniform dress for dancers

parts.note: tut is the clicking sound of disapproval
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone tuts at the matching outfits worn by a dance troupe.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutu is the stiff short skirt worn by ballerinas, a costume for dancers.

clue.text: Child chased by adder regularly in moorland the whole way

indicators.note: chased by means followed by, so the child comes first and the rest after

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: in places those kept letters inside the moorland word

parts.note: heath is open uncultivated moorland

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of adder

explanation.surface: A child on the moors is pursued by an adder all the way.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighting to the death means continuing to the very end, so the phrase means all the way, without stopping.

clue.text: Swimmer's time leading to defeat

indicators.note: leading to means coming in front of, so the time goes first

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: A competitive swimmer's slow time leads to their defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a competitor in a race; it is a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A trout is a freshwater fish, and fish are crossword swimmers.

clue.text: Grim quality of nasty sneers after end of Christmas Eve

indicators.note: something nasty is twisted out of its proper shape, so these letters are rearranged
the end of a word is its final letter alone, so only that is taken

parts.note: the last letter of Christmas
taken as written
the six letters of sneers rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sneers nastily on Christmas Eve, giving the evening a grim feel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the sneers anagram behind the end of Christmas and Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Severeness is the state of being severe, that is stern and grim in manner.

clue.text: Does exceptionally well gaining one gold and upwards

parts.note: to excel is to do exceptionally well
I is the Roman numeral one
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An athlete excels by winning a gold medal and moving up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gaining' adds the one and gold after the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Excelsior is a Latin motto meaning higher or ever upward, used as an exclamation of aspiration.

clue.text: Priest leaving bar incident

indicators.note: leaving means departing from, so the priest letters are taken out

parts.note: to bar is to prevent
Pr is the abbreviation for priest

explanation.surface: A clergyman walks out of a pub after some unpleasant scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub noun; it is the verb meaning stop.
explanation.definitionFit: An incident is an occurrence or happening, that is an event.

clue.text: English city demolishing round one area where Wedgwood worked

indicators.note: demolishing means knocking down and removing, so the round letter is removed from the city

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
Truro is the cathedral city of Cornwall
O is round in shape
I is the Roman numeral one
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: An English city is demolished around the area where the potter Wedgwood had his works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English city' looks like one unit, but English gives E and city alone is the Cornish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Etruria was Josiah Wedgwood's pottery works and village near Stoke-on-Trent, named after the ancient Italian region.

clue.text: Controlling river channel and river — not two rivers

indicators.note: not two tells us to drop a pair of things from the word before it

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
a cut is a dug channel or canal
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river, so two of them

explanation.surface: A water engineer controls a river channel while doing without two rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Executive as an adjective means having the power to manage or direct, as in executive powers.

clue.text: Staunch supporter of gardens

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to stop a flow, as of blood
second meaning: the stalk that holds up a plant's flowers and leaves

explanation.walkthrough: 'Staunch supporter' reads as a loyal fan; split it, and staunch is a verb on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem is to stanch a flow, and a stem is the plant stalk that holds up what grows in a garden.

clue.text: Drought reduced Yorkshire town over time

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the town loses its final letter
in a down clue over means above, so the town sits on top of the time

parts.note: Thirsk is a market town in North Yorkshire
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A drought shrinks a Yorkshire town's water supply over time.
explanation.definitionFit: Drought in an older sense means thirst, a dryness of the throat, as well as a lack of rain.

clue.text: Canine ailment? Oh, the coat is mangy

indicators.note: a mangy coat is ragged and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A vet diagnoses a dog's illness by its scruffy, mangy coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine' reads as doggy, but a canine is also a pointed tooth; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothache is pain in a tooth, and a canine is one of the pointed teeth, so a canine ailment.

clue.text: Old official always about arresting English

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for always runs backwards
arresting means seizing and holding, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An old official forever arresting Englishmen sounds like a hard-line constable.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed always word opens after its first two letters to take in E.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a medieval local magistrate or steward, an official in an English shire or manor.

clue.text: Hour joining a line by hospital department entrance

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
HR is the abbreviation for hour
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Directions in a hospital: queue an hour in a line by the department's entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like a doorway noun, but it is the verb meaning to put in a trance; 'joining' and 'by' arrange the pieces, with the department placed first.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to captivate or charm them completely, which is exactly what enthral means.

clue.text: Twist editor queried to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so only a portion of the following words is used

parts.note: sits across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An editor partly questions a twist in a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Torque is a twisting force, so the word stands for twist in mechanics.

clue.text: Neat and decent reformed prior

indicators.note: reformed means made over in a new form, so these letters are reorganised

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A tidy, respectable monastic prior who has mended his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prior' suggests a monk; here it is the adjective meaning earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Antecedent means coming before in time or order, a synonym of prior.

clue.text: Recite fictional broadcast adding points?

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, as seed is sown, so these letters are scattered

parts.note: the fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A radio reading of fiction that has had some points added to it.
explanation.walkthrough: Points here are electrical sockets, called power points in Britain; wiring a house adds them, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrification is supplying a building with electric power, which means installing power points or sockets.

clue.text: Gets piqued with its item requiring uncovering in protocol

indicators.note: uncovering strips off the outer layer, so each word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: the inner letters of gets
the inner letters of piqued
the inner letter of its
the inner letters of item

explanation.surface: Someone takes offence when an item has its cover removed during a formal ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the four words; all four are stripped.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiquette is the code of correct behaviour, and protocol is formal etiquette, as in diplomacy.

clue.text: Get involved to help bury Edward in church

parts.note: to inter is to bury

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A friend helps out at a funeral by burying Edward in the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To intercede is to step in on someone's behalf, getting involved in order to help them.

clue.text: What might blow up tent in another case using no energy?

definitions.text: What might blow up tent in another case using no energy?

parts.note: surface reading: something used to inflate a tent, in a different situation, without any effort

parts.words: tent in another case using no energy
parts.note: setter's reading: tent with no E is a three-letter abbreviation, here written out in full in a different case, small letters instead of capitals

explanation.surface: A camper wonders what might pump up a tent without needing any energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E (energy) from tent to get TNT, the explosive; TRINITROTOLUENE is TNT written out in another case, lower case and in full. 'Blow up' means explode, not inflate.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinitrotoluene is the full chemical name of TNT, a high explosive that would indeed blow things up.

clue.text: Repeat over and over — it takes a long time, note

parts.note: taken as written
an era is a long period of time
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Repeating something over and over takes ages, someone observes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes' joins IT to the long time; the note goes last.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to do or say something again and again, a formal word for repeating.

clue.text: Preparation of cells is behind, including last two in Strangeways

indicators.note: including means holding within, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: behind schedule means late

indicators.note: last two in asks for just the final pair of letters of the following word

parts.note: the final two letters of Strangeways

explanation.surface: Cell preparation is running behind in Strangeways prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Strangeways is a Manchester prison, so 'cells' looks like prison cells; they are biological ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A lysate is the fluid produced when cells are broken open, a laboratory preparation of cell contents.

clue.text: What's acceptable in clothing for imprisonment

indicators.note: something in clothing is wrapped up and enclosed, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: dress is clothing in general
U means upper-class and so socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A question about what counts as acceptable clothing for someone in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothing' does double duty in the reading: 'in clothing' places the acceptable letter inside the clothing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress in legal language includes unlawful constraint or imprisonment, besides its usual sense of coercion.

clue.text: Stalks bound to be mostly cut fine

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the cutting word is dropped

parts.note: to shear is to cut
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone stalks off, bound to have their hair cut finely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stalks' looks like a verb of walking; it is the noun, plant stems.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheaf is a bundle of cereal stalks tied together after reaping.

clue.text: Setter confused about round diamond

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around another piece
confused means muddled up, so these letters come out in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: The crossword setter is baffled by a round diamond.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a style of cut diamond, faceted on top with a flat base, as well as a ribbon badge.

clue.text: Exchange of invective I missed

indicators.note: missed means left out, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: a tirade is a long angry speech of invective
taken as written and removed

explanation.surface: An exchange of insults that one person failed to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade is buying and selling, the exchange of goods for money.

clue.text: Try one's luck introducing European vegetable

indicators.note: introducing means bringing in, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: to bet is to gamble, trying one's luck
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A gambler bets on bringing in a European vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Beet is a root vegetable, as in beetroot and sugar beet.

clue.text: Minor actor is remarkable, not ordinary

indicators.note: not tells us that the following word must be taken away from the longer word

parts.note: extraordinary means remarkable
taken as written and removed

explanation.surface: A walk-on actor turns out to be remarkable rather than ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a performer hired for a crowd scene with no lines, the most minor of film roles.

clue.text: Turn up day before new gallery closes in university

indicators.note: closes in means shuts around something, so the gallery surrounds the next piece

parts.note: the eve is the day before an event
N is the abbreviation for new
the Tate is the London art gallery
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: An instruction to arrive the day before a new gallery shuts down its university branch.
explanation.definitionFit: To eventuate is to happen as a result, which is what a thing does when it turns up or occurs.

clue.text: After that drug stashed in a specific roof beam

indicators.note: something stashed in a place is hidden inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a specific one is the one, and a rafter is a sloping roof beam
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: After that, drugs were found hidden in a particular beam of the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A specific' turns the indefinite article into THE, the definite one.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereafter is a formal adverb meaning from that time on, after that.

clue.text: Retained cap, changing bits of it?

indicators.note: one letter of the word it is swapped for the other letter of it

parts.note: a kepi is a French military cap with a flat top and peak

explanation.surface: Someone holds on to a cap but swaps parts of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The bits of 'it' are I and T: the I at the end of the cap becomes T.
explanation.definitionFit: Kept is the past tense of keep, meaning held on to or retained.
